==Proto-Semitic==

===Etymology===
Reconstructed in Militarev & Kogan's ''Semitic Etymological Dictionary'' as {{m|sem-pro|*ʕakbar-}}. The SED also compares several terms with metathesis, meaning shifts or secondary emphasis, such as Syriac {{m|syc|ܥܘܩܒܪܐ|tr=ʕuḳbərā}} and the Modern South Arabian forms like Mehri {{m|gdq|ʔārḳáyb}}.
